what: The shared .github/actions/blaze action installs stage 0 through the Unix shell installer and its LLVM setup rejects Windows, so using it for the first Windows release is circular.
cost: The first Windows archive job would fail before building anything and could never create the archive that the action would need on its next run.
cause: Release bootstrap assumed every shipping platform already had an archive consumable by site/install.sh.
whys: The action installs a released blaze; the released blaze has no Windows asset; the Unix installer refuses Windows; the action also has no Windows LLVM case; therefore adding Windows only to the release matrix cannot bootstrap the first native artifact.
class: A new release platform depending on its own not-yet-existing release artifact.
prevention: A new platform's recipe must name its stage-0 path separately and prove that the shipped stage is rebuilt by blaze; once a released Windows blaze is pinned, the shared action can take over.
workaround: Build only stage 0 with the pinned nightly and pinned LLVM, then have that blaze build the release artifact.
fix: release.yaml now makes a pinned-nightly Windows stage 0 and build_release.py uses it to produce and validate the shipped Windows stage.
